articleTitle: Coherently coupled high power fiber arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A four-element fiber array has demonstrated 470 watts of coherently phased, linearly polarized light. The results of this experiment as well as comparisons to other fiber array approaches will be presented

articleTitle: Afterpulsing in InGaAs/InP single photon avalanche photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The effect of short gating pulses on after-pulsing in a single photon avalanche photodetector operating at a telecom wavelength of 1.5 mum is characterized and discussed. Comparison between short and longer overbias gate pulses shows that the number of carriers created with a 1 ns (short) gating pulse is lower than that of a 20 ns pulse, when the avalanche is dark-count generated

articleTitle: The HgCdTe electron avalanche photodiode
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper reports results obtained on mid-wave, short-wave, and long-wave cutoff infrared Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te EAPDs that utilize a cylindrical "p-around-n", front side illuminated, n+/n-/p geometry that favors electron injection into the gain region. These devices are characterized by a uniform, exponential, gain voltage characteristic that is consistent with a hole-to-electron ionization coefficient ratio, of zero

articleTitle: An InGaAs/InP photodiode with 600 mW RF output power
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report an InGaAs/InP charge compensated uni-traveling-carrier photodiode with thick depletion region with RF output power of 600 mW at 2 GHz.

articleTitle: Polarization effects in polarization-independent and polarization maintaining fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Polarization effects in fiber optical amplifiers are described. Theoretical and experimental results for the statistical variation of the polarization extinction ratio (PER) in a PM amplifier are presented. PER variation between units and over temperature is analyzed

articleTitle: Architecture, security and topology of a global Quantum Key Distribution network
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The performances of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems have notably progressed since the early experimental demonstrations and several recent works indicate that the pace of this progression is very likely to be maintained -if not increased- in the future years. In parallel to this fast progression of QKD techniques, commercial products are also being developed, making QKD deployment for securization of some specific “real” data networks more and more likely to occur. It is the goal to the European project Secoqc to deploy a secure long-distance network based on quantum cryptography. It implies the conception of a specific architecture able to connect multiple users that may possibly be very far away from each other while QKD links are currently ″point-to-point only″and intrinsically limited in distance.

articleTitle: Large format HgCdTe arrays for the James Webb Space Telescope
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The near infrared spectrograph (NIRSpec) will be the James Webb Space Telescope's (JWSTs) primary near-infrared spectrograph. NIRSpec is a multi-object spectrograph with fixed-slit and integral field modes. EADS/Astrium is building NIRSpec for the European Space Agency (ESA), with NASA providing the detector subsystem and programmable multi-aperture mask. In this presentation we present an overview of the detector subsystem (DS)

articleTitle: High-power photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Recent progress in high current photodiodes now makes it possible to linearly detect over 250 mA at frequencies into X Band. This paper will discuss the recent improvements that have lead to this dramatic improvement.

articleTitle: Bi-based fibers for amplifiers and nonlinear applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper short pulse amplification of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3 </sub> based erbium-doped fiber (BIEDF) and high nonlinearity of Bi-NLF are reported

articleTitle: Spatial cell discrimination using optoelectronic tweezers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The difference in dielectric properties of live HeLa and Jurkat cells are used to spatially discriminate the cells using optoelectronic tweezers. Spatial discrimination is verified by fluorescent tagging of the Jurkat cells.

articleTitle: Avalanche diodes and circuits for infrared photon counting and timing: retrospect and prospect
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The evolution of single-photon avalanche diodes (SPAD) and associated avalanche-quenching circuits for extending beyond 1 micron wavelength the spectral range of photon counting and timing is reviewed and the prospect of further progress is discussed

articleTitle: First demonstration of 10 microns FPAs in InAs/GaSb superlattices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on InAs/GaSb superlattice as an emerging infrared material for developing the focal plane arrays (FPAs). An initial demonstration using this material for FPA mesa formation is discussed

articleTitle: A reconfigurable microfluidic platform in ice
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this research a CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> IR laser was used to create reconfigurable microchannels in ice where parameters could be changed during operation. The flow of liquid acts as its own shut-off valve by freezing/melting. Concentration of dye can be achieved in ice and was observed with a reflection spectrophotometer

articleTitle: Optofluidic tuning and sensing in fiber based devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review progress in optofluidics performed using optical fibers as the photonic transport medium. We fluidically tune the transmission properties of microstructured optical fibers and use telecommunications fibers to probe the optical properties of fluids

articleTitle: Acoustical-optical fibers for control of stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present recent modeling and experimental results, and a discussion of practical issues on the design and fabrication of SBS-suppressed optical fibers for lasers and nonlinear applications employing fibers without rare earth dopants

articleTitle: Pulsed high power fiber laser systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The master-oscillator power-amplifier approach, cladding pumping technology and large mode area fibers provide a route to compact and efficient pulsed fiber laser systems with high beam quality and high output powers

articleTitle: Chiral fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Examples of adiabatic modification of optical fiber parameters while maintaining single-mode propagation are discussed in the paper. It is found that adiabatic variation of polarization of fiber mode enables efficient coupling of a PM fiber supporting linearly polarized modes and a chiral fiber supporting circularly or elliptically polarized modes

articleTitle: 4/spl times/4 individually addressable InGaAs APD arrays optimized for photon counting applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: InGaAs APDs with improved photon counting characteristics were designed and fabricated and their performance improvements were observed. Following the results, a 4/spl times/4 individually addressable APD array was designed, fabricated, and results are reported.

articleTitle: Large effective mode area fibers for high power lasers and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: New progress for novel design for achieving large effective mode area fibers while maintaining single mode operation for fiber lasers and fibre amplifiers is addressed in the presentation

articleTitle: Bacteria detection in a microfluidic channel utilizing electromagnetic cellular polarization and optical scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A bacterial detection scheme based on aligning the bacteria with an electric field and detecting the optical scattering is examined. This method uses no biochemical markers and can be applied in a point-of-care setting.

articleTitle: Algorithmic tunability of quantum-dot infrared detectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, recent developments in post-processing techniques for quantum-dot infrared detectors (QDIPs) and provide spectral tuning and classification examples that show potential capability of QDIPs as hyperspectral and multispectral sensors

articleTitle: Improvement of the properties of a variable focus elastic lens by finite element optimization
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The concept of a variable focus elastic lens has been examined. Optimization of the geometry of a soft core in the lens improved the optical properties compared to a monolithic lens.

articleTitle: Practical quantum key distribution systems based on faint laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, the functioning and the performance of the auto-compensated quantum cryptography system developed is presented. The optical apparatus, as well as the hardware platform controlling it is described. The protocol allowing to distill a secret key from a raw key and practical applications of quantum cryptography are discussed

articleTitle: Recent advances in avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on recent work on avalanche photodiodes (APDs) which focused on developing new structures and incorporating alternative materials that will yield lower excess noise and higher speed while maintaining optimal gain levels

articleTitle: Geiger-mode avalanche photodiodes for laser communications and laser radar
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Arrays of photon-counting avalanche photodiodes (APDs) enable laser-communications and laser-radar receivers with unprecedented sensitivity at 1.06-mum wavelength. Near room temperature, the best detectors have: 50% photon detection efficiency, 30-kHz dark count rate, and a 1-mus reset time to avoid after-pulsing. Arrays with 64 elements were fabricated in the InGaAsP/InP materials system and were bump-bonded to a custom CMOS integrated circuit (IC) with a novel nonblocking architecture to continuously report both time-of-arrival for incoming photons as well as their spatial location on the array. Larger arrays with 1024 elements were mated to custom read-out ICs that report time and location data at lower duty cycles (typically 1-5%) and are appropriate for pulsed laser-radar systems

articleTitle: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present our ongoing work on superconducting NbN-nanowire photodetectors, which deliver both high speed (< 30 ps timing resolution) and high detection efficiency (> 50% at 1550 nm), promising access to new regimes in ultrafast photon counting applications

articleTitle: Gigahertz clocked quantum key distribution in passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Two multi-user approaches to fiber-based quantum key distribution systems operating at gigahertz clock frequencies are presented, both compatible with standard telecommunications fiber

articleTitle: A novel pump combiner for high power fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A new type of combiner is proposed that permits the efficient introduction of multimode diode pump radiation in a distributed manner along the fiber, which can lead to lower thermal loading. The coupling efficiency is expected to be high, and in addition, this coupler reduces the amount of signal radiation damaging the diodes

articleTitle: Optofluidic microscope: a novel high resolution microscope-on-a- chip system
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, a novel on-chip optical imaging device, termed optofluidic microscope (OFM) is presented, which features compact size and high resolution along with high-speed imaging.

articleTitle: Large core polymer waveguides for optical backplanes in microfluidic systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A platform is developed which utilizes polymer materials used for the chips to create waveguide based optical components. With the fabrication method demonstrated, waveguides, power splitters, combiners and bends can be introduced and integrated cheaply into existing biochips

articleTitle: On-chip detection with nanohole arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A microfluidic device with an embedded surface-plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor array was developed. The sensing elements are nanohole arrays, differentiated by periodicity. On-chip chemical detection using SPR is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic tweezers for particle and cell manipulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Optoelectronic tweezers is a new tool for parallel optical manipulation of colloids and cells. Using a digital projector to pattern dynamic virtual electrodes on a photoconductive surface, we demonstrate parallel trapping, transporting, and sorting of micro/bio-particles.

articleTitle: Security and efficiency of quantum cryptographic protocols
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: For concrete quantum key generation and quantum direct encryption protocols, we discuss the various problems in quantifying the security level and the efficiency associated with the steps of advantage creation, error correction, and privacy amplification

articleTitle: And God said, let there be confidentiality
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: After a brief historical perspective on quantum cryptography, this essay asks the question: Why should perfect confidentiality be possible according to quantum mechanics, but not perfect bit commitment? For the sake of liveliness, the style is purposely that of a spontaneous after-dinner speech

articleTitle: Conversion of photon spin to electron spin for quantum repetition
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Coherent spin transfer from photons to electrons is a key process in semiconductor quantum repeaters. We discuss experimental progress towards this goal, including the capture, detection and storage of single photoelectrons in GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures.

articleTitle: Wavelength conversion in highly nonlinear single mode As/sub 2/Se/sub 3/ chalcogenide fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We establish design criteria for pump-probe devices in two photon absorbing materials and demonstrate low-power wavelength conversion over 10 nm in 1 m of single mode As/sub 2/Se/sub 3/ fiber through cross-phase modulation with only 1.4 dB system penalty at BER = 10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Microfluidic-based optical controls for on-chip optical tweezers and microbubble formation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: By using on-chip lenses and fluidic operations to control focal length and direction of a laser beam, two kind of new concepts are proposed in the paper. One is a device to generate and control micro bubbles inside a microfluidic chip. Second is a new optical paths control method by microfluidic operation. To demonstrate the functionality of the optical paths control, the present method was utilized for optical tweezers applications

articleTitle: Architectures for quantum networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper discusses on current status of quantum key distribution (QKD) networking and suggests some potential network architectures

articleTitle: Quantum telecommunication
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on recent work aimed at quantum networks with atomic ensembles.

articleTitle: Differential-phase-shift quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A novel type of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol called differential-phase-shift (DPS) QKD is described. It utilizes a weak coherent pulse train instead of individual photons as in conventional QKD

articleTitle: Photon counting detectors for quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Advances in semiconductor single photon avalanche diode detectors have enabled expanding application areas in the near-infrared. This presentation will discuss their performance, potential and their use in applications such as quantum key distribution

articleTitle: Tunable long period gratings in fluid-filled photonic bandgap fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Fluid filled photonic bandgap fibers (PBGFs) incorporate materials with a large dn/dT. The modes of these fibers are also strongly dispersive. We exploit these properties of PBGFs to demonstrate highly tunable long period gratings.

articleTitle: Bend resistance of large-mode-area higher-order-mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Higher-order-mode fibers with very large mode area are shown to be naturally resistant to bend induced mode distortion, an important limitation on amplifier fibers. Simulations and measurements display resistance of these fibers to bending

articleTitle: Diamond single photon sources
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We are currently developing a diamond single photon source based on patented technology held at the University of Melbourne. The key technology is the growth of diamond nanocrystals containing single photon sources directly on optical fibre endfaces

articleTitle: Optofluidic microsorter: an integrated flow cytometry instrument for cell biology applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The authors have built a high-throughput, fluorescence-activated microfluidic cell sorter based on an active, all-optical particle control switch. After being aligned to the center of the channel by flow focusing, cells are analyzed and then switched based on their detected fluorescence. Target cells are directed by the laser to the collection output while all other cells flow to the waste output.

articleTitle: Optical tweezers and optofluidics
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, the authors demonstrated the use of optically trapped microspheres to tune the transmission properties of embedded fiber optic waveguides, and the use of optical tweezers for optical actuation of cantilevers for use as switches and sensors

articleTitle: Multi-MW peak power, multi-mJ pulse energy Yb-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report on large-core, Yb-doped photonic crystal fibers used in gain-staged optical pulse amplifiers to generate ~ 1 ns pulses that simultaneously exhibit multi-MW peak power, multi-mJ pulse energy, near-diffraction-limited beam quality, and narrow spectral linewidth

articleTitle: All-fiber source of polarization-entangled photon pairs based on a novel birefringence compensated scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We propose a new all-fiber source of polarization-entangled photon pairs for quantum communications. Fiber birefringence is compensated using Faraday rotator mirror, resulting in enhanced stability against random polarization drifts compared to existing schemes.

articleTitle: Quantum well infrared photodetectors - recent advances at NRC
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Recent advances on quantum well infrared photodetectors (QWIP) at the National Research Council Canada are reviewed. These include the demonstration of QWIP-LED pixelless imaging, the development of THz, ultrafast, and two-photon QWIPs

articleTitle: Mid infrared InP-based photodiodes operating at/near room temperature
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This research aims to develop InP-based devices as alternative for MWIR detection. The approach pursued is a type-II superlattice consisting GaInAs and GaAsSb alloys. These structures provide two advantages for MWIR detection: large (greater than 700 meV) direct band-gaps, which should lead to a lower thermal carrier generation rate and the ability to adjust the detection wavelength by changing the compositions of GaInAs and GaAsSb and their thickness, in the superlattice

articleTitle: Optofluidic particle manipulation and characterization in nanowell sensors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We describe the development of "electroactive" nanowells which exploit extremely localized electrokinetic effects in order to guide and confine nanoparticles into targeted nanostructures. Applications for the devices include sensing and optofluidically adaptable photonics.

articleTitle: Optimization of ultrafast chirped-pulse amplification with large nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The mechanism of chirped-pulse amplification performance improvement with interplay of nonlinearity and third-order dispersion is successfully interpreted with a simple theoretical model. One can extract design parameters optimizing the output performance according to the model

articleTitle: Manipulating time-bin qubits with fiber optics components
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We propose two experimental schemes to implement arbitrary unitary single qubit operations on single photons encoded in time-bin qubits. Both schemes require fiber optics components that are available with current technology

articleTitle: Quantum dot infrared detectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Quantum dot infrared photodetectors have emerged as viable devices capable of normal incidence operation over wide wavelength range at high temperatures. The latest results in the development of these devices will be presented and discussed

articleTitle: Toward, single molecule detection with photonic crystal microcavity biosensors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Time resolved biomolecular binding events were measured using photonic crystal microcavity resonators integrated with microfluidics. The optical field is confined to a volume of 33 /spl times/ 10/sup -18/ liters, which enables monitoring of single binding events.

articleTitle: Self-synchronous coherent beam combination
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A completely novel concept for coherent beam combination is presented. The technique completely eliminates the need for a reference beam resulting in a dramatic simplification of electronic coherent beam combination without any compromise in performance

articleTitle: Single-molecule optofluidics using liquid-core ARROW waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review recent development of liquid-core ARROW waveguides for combining planar integrated optics and microfluidics on a chip. Optical design, microfabrication, and optical characterization are presented, including demonstration of single molecule fluorescence sensitivity

articleTitle: Dynamic microfluidic photomasking
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper presents a novel microfluidic photomasking strategy. Multi-layer laminar microfluidic streaming is exploited to achieve photomasking with dynamic spatial control. Applications to microarray and photoresist patterning are investigated

articleTitle: Comb-like profiled fiber technologies for synchronized short pulse generation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review our recent results on optical short pulse generation based on "comb-like profiled fiber (CPF)". Various types of CPF are summarized, where we show that the CPF technologies are suitable for truly practical, externally synchronous, and flexible short pulse generation

articleTitle: Fiber lasers with phosphate photonic crystal and multicore fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Active phosphate photonic crystal (PC) fibers with large fundamental mode areas have been demonstrated for miniature high-power high-brightness and single frequency fiber lasers at 1.5 mum

articleTitle: Recent developments in infrared phosphors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The preparation and characterization nanophosphors and their usage as IR detectors in various applications are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Optofluidics for adaptation and sensing
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper presents some of their recent works on optofluidics for adaptation and sensing applications. Demonstrated microfluidic-based adaptive optical devices are all optical switch based on control of total internal reflection (TIR) and microring resonator device (MRD)

articleTitle: Joint supermode and LP01 passive mode selection in an array of large mode area fiber lasers using a compact self Fourier cavity
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper presents results based on detailed analysis showing that large numbers of emitting elements can be coherently combined by using spontaneous phase locking of fiber lasers and that smaller numbers of high-power, large mode area (LMA) elements can be combined to achieve very high output power

articleTitle: Interdigitated photodiode fabricated on high quality Ge on Si with thin SiGe buffer layers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An interdigitated Ge-on-Si photodetector has been fabricated, and achieved 73% quantum efficiency at 1.3 mum. The internal quantum efficiency is close to unity due to the high quality Ge film grown with thin SiGe buffer layers

articleTitle: Recent advances in pulsed fiber lasers passively mode-locked by carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review our recent works on passively mode-locked lasers functioned by carbon nanotubes. Researches are focused on the diversified structures of the nanotube mode-lockers as well as the ultrashort laser cavity configurations for telecom applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of a continuous phase-only sampling for 81-channel fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, a novel continuous phase-only sampling function is introduced, in which optimization for an 81-channel phase-only sampling function with excellent channel uniformity and high in-band energy efficiency is obtained by using the simulated annealing algorithm. Compared to the numerical results, an 81-channel (spacing 50 GHz) phase-only sampled linearly chirped FBG are successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of very low dark current SWIR PIN arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Two approaches to reducing the dark current are presented to modify the epitaxial material to reduce the bulk diffusion dark current and to modify the PIN design to minimize the impact of generation current. In addition, material and device characterization data that contrast these approaches to the earlier conventional approaches will be discussed

articleTitle: High-sensitivity scattering-based detection under symmetrical arrayed-waveguide platform
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Scattering-based on-chip excitation and detection under arrayed-waveguide platform have been developed and implemented. Through the signal-processing algorithm, amplified, and subsequently verified, signals can be used to detect particles of different velocities.

articleTitle: Microfluidic dye laser chip for intra-cavity absorption measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Among many others, absorbance measurement is one of the most useful techniques to determine sample concentration on a microfluidic chip. The main drawback of this technique comes from the limited optical path length that can be achieved on a chip. We propose here an original design of a microfluidic dye laser to perform intracavity absorption measurements. The effective optical path length and so the sensitivity are enhanced by a factor of about 15 in comparison with single pass measurement. In addition, the nanoliter active sample volume we used is six orders of magnitude less in comparison with common milliliter cuvette. Simple calculations that emphasize the potential utility of the method are also presented

articleTitle: Slow light via stimulated Brillouin scattering in optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Optical-fiber-based slow-light techniques are reviewed. Slow light via stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in optical fibers is discussed and recent progress in achieving broadband SBS slow light for high data-rate systems is presented.

articleTitle: Microfluidic dye lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A technology for miniaturized, polymer based lasers, suitable for integration with planar waveguides and microfluidic networks is presented. The microfluidic dye laser device consists of a microfluidic channel with an embedded optical resonator. The devices are fabricated in a thin polymer film sandwiched between two glass substrates. The devices are defined in the 1-10 mum thick polymer film by photolithography, nanoimprinting or by electron beam lithography, and the lid is bonded using adhesive polymer bonding

articleTitle: Optofluidic tuning of quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The authors demonstrate the compatibility of quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) with elastomer-based microfluidics and the tuning of QCLs using liquids with different refractive indices. They look to increasing sensitivity to liquids with ultra high-Q photonic crystal based QCLs.

articleTitle: Microspheres-fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Doped silica microspheres are used to build a novel, rugged, and tunable laser system. The microspheres are adhered to a fiber by a refractive index matching glow and pumped from one end of the fiber

articleTitle: Quantum communication in standard optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Quantum cryptography, quantum teleportation and experiments on entanglement is reviewed with special emphasize on the state of the art and the challenges of the 5-10 next years

articleTitle: Optofluidic intracavity spectroscopy for single cell detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Spectra of single biological cells including yeast cells and human blood cells using the optofluidic resonant cavity are reported in this work. A method for spectral correlation is also presented to verify the preliminary results of the single cell spectra. The correlation calculation demonstrates that the method is able to differentiate some types of single cells

articleTitle: Dispersion decreasing photonic crystal fiber for UV-enhanced supercontinuum generation
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We have fabricated a photonic crystal fiber with a continuously decreasing zero-dispersion wavelength along its length. It has been used to generate an ultraviolet-extended supercontinuum from a nanosecond pump source at 1.064 mum

articleTitle: New directions in optical trapping with microfluidics
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An overview of novel methods for creating optical traps and optical landscapes for performing optical sorting experiments in both microfluidic flows and static geometries as well as deploying novel sources and forms of light beams for biophysics is presented

articleTitle: Practical quantum communications for telecom networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present latest results on developing telecom-band resources for practical quantum communications in wave-division-multiplexed optical networks. Progress on in-fiber entanglement generation/distribution and quantum-noise-randomized direct data encryption will be described

articleTitle: Quantum networking with trapped atomic ions
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reviews the several methods for networking trapped ion qubits, and speculates the future of creating networks of entangled trapped atomic ions through Coulombic or photonic coupling

articleTitle: Differential phase shift quantum key distribution with up-conversion single-photon detectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A differential phase shift quantum key distribution experiment employing up-conversion single-photon detectors is presented. We achieved a 1-Mbit/s sifted key rate over a 20-km optical fiber, and distributed keys secure against general individual attacks over 75 km

articleTitle: Quantum information processing with quantum dot-photonic crystal devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An inverse problem approach to designing photonic crystal cavities is reviewed. The theoretical and experimental work on integration of a number of photonic crystal components (cavities and waveguides) into functional circuits for quantum information processing, including nontrivial two-qubit quantum gates is also reviewed.

articleTitle: Colour centres in diamond as practical single-photon sources
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper describes a "turn-key" single-photon source based on nitrogen-vacancy (N-V) colour centre photoluminescence inside dispersed diamond nanocrystals. The authors have used the emitted single photons to realize a wave-particle delayed-choice experiment based on a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The diamond-based single-photon source is also to open-air quantum key distribution (QKD).

articleTitle: A high-performance single photon avalanche detector for telecom wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>As/InP avalanche photodiode with very high performance (dark count rate = 12 kHz and single photon detection efficiency = 45% at 1.3 mum and 200 K) is reported

articleTitle: Particle transport in liquid core photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Here we describe the optical guidance and transport of particles in a liquid-core photonic crystal fiber (PCF). Immediate possible applications of our work include bioanalytical separation and sensing

articleTitle: Terahertz microfluidics for on-chip detection and identification of biomolecular compositions and conformations
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, the authors demonstrated that microfluidic devices can be used to perform on-chip THz spectroscopy of biomolecules and chemical agents with high signal-to-noise ratios

articleTitle: Network architectures for QKD
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present two schemes for QKD network architectures based on two ubiquitous topologies: the tree and the ring. Quantum key addressing schemes and their implications are also discussed.

articleTitle: Fiber-based degenerate correlated-photon source in the telecom band
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate a fiber-based correlated-photon source, wherein the two daughter photons are degenerate in frequency. A coincidence-to-accidental-coincidence ratio >100 is obtained when the fiber is cooled to liquid nitrogen temperature

articleTitle: Optical and near-infrared photon detection with superconducting transition-edge sensors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: There is increasing interest in using high-performance cryogenic optical photon detectors in a variety of applications in quantum information science and technology. These applications require detectors that have extremely low dark count rates, high photon count rates, high quantum efficiency, and moderate energy resolution or photon number resolution for near-infrared and optical photons. In this paper, we describe the operation, fabrication, and performance of superconducting transition-edge sensors designed for quantum optics and information applications.

articleTitle: Progress on MBE grown type-II superlattice photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on the status of type-II superlattice diodes grown and fabricated for infrared absorption in the mid- and long wavelength infrared ranges. Recent progress in epitaxial regrowth as a passivation method and progress on long-wavelength imaging array fabrication are also presented

articleTitle: Investigations of an erbium doped optical fiber for quantum state storage
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We study optical coherence properties and Stark-shift based broadening of the 1.53 /spl mu/m transition of an erbium doped telecommunication fiber. Our findings demonstrate its potential for quantum state storage as required for a quantum repeater.

articleTitle: Noise modeling in quantum IR photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The limits of validity of the g-r approach addressing a few specific features of the quantum photodetector noise are discussed. To describe the photodetection process in quantum well infrared photodetectors, the standard model valid for homogeneous semiconductors including the simple generation-recombination noise mechanisms, have been adopted relying on charge relaxation dynamics occurring via a simple exponential process

articleTitle: A novel type-II infrared single photon detector
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A novel infrared single photon detector for wavelengths above 1 mum is presented. It incorporates novel carrier focalization and nanoinjection. A finite element method based simulation is implemented to model and verify predicted superior performance

articleTitle: Using optical forces for the characterization of biological cell activities
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Optical forces successfully manipulate biological cells and measure small forces such as molecular binding forces. This paper focuses on the use of optical forces for the direct characterization of various activities of biological cells

articleTitle: Interplay of nonlinearity and gain-shaping in high-energy femtosecond Yb-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Spectral shaping in a fiber amplifier in the presence of finite gain bandwidth (15 nm) and large nonlinear phase shifts (up to /spl sim/12 /spl phi/) is studied numerically and experimentally. Pulses amplified to 30 /spl mu/J are dechirped to /spl sim/250 fs duration.

articleTitle: Sagnac quantum key distribution using novel polarization-insensitive phase modulators based on frequency shift
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate a stable Sagnac quantum key distribution implementing BB84 phase-encoding protocol based on acousto-optic frequency shifters. The quantum bit error rate remains 4-6.5% for at least one hour without recalibration or feedback control.

articleTitle: Infrared focal plane arrays based on quantum dots and strain layer superlattices
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on the fabrication of focal plane arrays using two material systems for mid infrared sensors. These are InAs/InGaAs self assembled quantum dots in well (DWELL) and InAs/(In,Ga)Sb strain layer superlattices (SLS) detectors.

articleTitle: Silicon-based photonic crystal biosensors
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, the optical response of 1-D and 2-D Si photonic crystal (PC) is investigated after exposure to various chemical and biological targets. PBG biosensors made of porous silicon have been demonstrated, in particular they have been used to selectively detect DNA, proteins and bacteria

articleTitle: Generation of ten-cycle pulses from a Yb fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a prism-grating sequence to reduce third-order dispersion inside a modelocked Yb fiber laser. 33-fs pulses, the shortest from a fiber oscillator, can be generated with extremely clean profiles

articleTitle: First experimental demonstration of coherent fiber array phase locking without an external reference beam
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A 3/spl times/3 passive fiber and a 3/spl times/2 fiber amplifier arrays were phase locked using two novel phase locking architectures. The measured phase error was /spl lambda//22 independent of the number of elements locked.

articleTitle: Modeling hot electron in single quantum well p-i-n photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A detailed formulation of energy balance equation is presented. The AlGaAs/GaAs QW results show that hot carrier effect can influence the I-V characteristics for devices with long relaxation lifetime at high injection level. Comparisons made with the available measured data support the modeling of QW p-i-n AlGaAs/GaAs photodiode structures

articleTitle: Laser-induced fluorescence photobleaching anemometer for flow velocity measurement in sub-microscale fluidic channels
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A non-particle tracing technique based on laser-induced fluorescence photobleaching is demonstrated for measuring the flow velocity in microfluidic channels. The technique can give high spatial and temporal resolution in the measurement of velocity in microfluidic channels

articleTitle: Fluid optical waveguides for on-chip manipulation and generation of light
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Application of liquid-core liquid-cladding waveguides in several dynamic photonic systems. These optical components could be reconfigured in terms of their geometry, refractive index, or chemical composition

articleTitle: Spatial and temporal stability of an N-core evanescently coupled fiber amplifier ring
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This work extends previous spatial stability analysis of an N-element ring-shaped amplifier array to include both time and position dependence. Coupled-mode equations the fields and populations are solved in steady state for the N supermodes, providing simple expressions for the gain, power, and propagation constants for each supermode. The technique then followed is to consider the time evolution of an arbitrary but small perturbation added to any one of the supermode solutions

articleTitle: Photodetectors for the 2-5 /spl mu/m spectral range based on III-V heterojunctions
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The design, fabrication and characterization of heterojunction photodiodes for room temperature operation in the mid-infrared (2-5 mum) spectral range is described. Devices appropriate for methane and carbon monoxide detection have been developed and studied

articleTitle: High performing photodiodes for demanding applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Demanding applications like laser range finding, proximity fuses, laser designation, smart munitions and laser warning systems all have the following in common i) detecting short pulses of light and the more sensitive the detector the better, ii) ability to operate in harsh environments and over a wide temperature range, iii) requirement for large dynamic range. In this paper we will examine how to design modules and package these photodiodes for these applications. In particular we will focus on InGaAs APD's for laser range finding, and on an InGaAs PIN array for a laser-warning module.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of coupled nanofluidic dynamics and silicon-on-insulator particle trapping
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Applications in integrated optical/fluidic systems require a fundamental understanding of coupling between optical and fluid dynamics in nanoscale systems. We use finite-element methods to examine the coupling of a silicon-on-insulator waveguide in microfluidic channels

articleTitle: High-energy femtosecond fiber lasers based on self-similar pulse evolution
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Theoretical and experimental advances in high-energy femtosecond fiber lasers will be reviewed. A new kind of pulse-formation based on self-similar propagation allows substantial increases in pulse energy compared to prior fiber lasers

articleTitle: Biological detectors using ultra-high-Q microresonators
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Ultra-high Q toroidal resonators have demonstrated the ability to maintain Q > 100 million in an aqueous environment. These quality factors enable ultra-sensitive detection of D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sub>O (1 ppmv) and biological molecules

articleTitle: Mechanically tunable optofluidic distributed feedback dye laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrated a continuously tunable optofluidic distributed feedback (DFB) dye laser on a monolithic poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) chip. We obtained ~60 nm tuning range by mechanically varying the grating period. Single-mode operation was maintained with <0.1 nm linewidth

articleTitle: Applications of higher order modes in optical fibers to femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Higher order modes in optical fiber present unique possibilities in terms of designing fibers for femtosecond pulse applications. A large mode area fiber using higher order modes with an effective area of 2100 mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is shown to allow for linear transmission of 14 nJ, femtosecond pulses

articleTitle: Generation of orbital vortices in optical fiber via acousto-optic interaction
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, it is shown that an acousto-optic interaction in optical fiber can lead to a transfer of orbital angular momentum (OAM) from an acoustic vortex to an optical vortex and that spin and orbital angular momentum are conserved independently in this interaction

articleTitle: Fabrication of third order Bragg gratings by UV nanoimprint lithography for optofluidic lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Soft UV nanoimprint lithography has be used to fabricate third order Bragg gratings for visible light and microfluidic dye laser operation. Soft stamps has been made by casting a poly-dimethylsiloxane on a silicon mould and a bi-layer imprinting process has used to obtain resist patterns of high density and high aspect ration line-and-space features. After a lift-off of thin nickel film, reactive ion etching was applied to transfer the patterned features into a glass substrate with aspect ratios up to 12. The integration of the fabricated Bragg gratings into a microfluidic chip allowed us to observe laser emission from a dye molecule (Rhodamine 6G) solution of very small volumes (30 to 75 pL), thereby providing a new method of making functioning optofluidic devices

articleTitle: Broadband emission from glass-clad chromium doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Broadband emission was generated with a 3-dB bandwidth of 406 nm at a center wavelength of 1140 nm by chromium doped fiber. This broadband emission is attributed to emission centers of Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in high-field site (HFS) and Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup> in both HFS and low-field site (LFS) when excited by 900-nm pumping wavelength

articleTitle: Practical one-way quantum cryptographic system for telecom networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present a one-way quantum key distribution system with active phase compensation. The system is characterized by a quantum bit error rate of 2.23% and a secure key rate of 24.4 kbps

articleTitle: Micro-fluidic photonic crystal vertical cavity surface emitting laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper reports on a monolithic microfluidic photonic crystal VCSEL wherein the fluid channels are both horizontal and vertical within the laser cavity. The photonic crystal pattern serves the dual purpose of acting as the vertical micro-channels and to produce single mode laser operation

articleTitle: Optimization of low noise continuum generation from femtosecond fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The paper describes two approaches for minimization of phase noise of the comb generated from a mode-locked fiber laser. First is the implementation of higher speed actuators for control of the comb and second is direct generation of an octave of continuum.

articleTitle: Fibers for Lasers, Amplifiers and Nonlinear Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Lists participants in select conference proceedings sessions.

articleTitle: Table of contents
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The following topics were dealt with: optical tweezers; optical fluidics in fibers; detection and imaging; photonic crystal detection; optofluidic lasers (dye lasers); quantum cryptography; photon-matter conversion; quantum communication system research and quantum network architectures

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2006 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
